label: On the word right after me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'of', 'my' or 'our') when a judgement bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us judging another person or group (labelling them, seeing them as something, praising, blaming, thanking, admiring, criticising, rewarding, punishing or forgiving them), and a following clause has that person or group return the same kind of judgement to me or us. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a one-way judgement of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us judged first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action that is not a judgement (visiting, phoning, paying, lending, hugging back); a judgement aimed at a thing rather than a person.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: The 'as', or the 'a' right after me, us or you, when a label bounces back at me, us or you: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, calling, regarding, treating or describing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group label me, us or you in return, either with 'as' (they saw me as a fool) or bare with 'a' (he called me a liar). Weaker: the same two-way swap between named people or third-person pronouns. Weak: a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause; me labelled first and then answering back; a plural bare return with no 'as' or 'a' (named us cowards); a return aimed at a third party; official appointments to a post.
